text:
Mia Chen: Heads up — running the async Python SDK in pytest (pytest-asyncio / anyio) and I'm hitting RuntimeError: Event loop is closed when the test suite finishes. Also reproducible in a Jupyter notebook. Anyone seen this?

Sam Ortega: can you paste a tiny repro? which Python / httpx / httpcore versions?

Mia Chen: minimal test:
```python
import pytest
from redwood import AsyncClient

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_embed():
    client = AsyncClient(api_key="fake")
    resp = await client.embed("hi")
    await client.aclose()
    assert resp
```
Error stack has: RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
Trace shows something calling asyncio.run in atexit or destructor path.

Alex K.: rough guess: our async client might be trying to close the loop with run_until_complete in __del__ or using get_event_loop() incorrectly. pytest-asyncio provides its own running loop and closing it from inside the SDK can blow up. What Python + httpx versions?

Mia Chen: Python 3.11.6, httpx 0.24.1, httpcore 0.16.0. Using the latest pip wheel of the SDK (0.9.3-beta).

Sam Ortega: for now workarounds: 1) use the async context manager (async with AsyncClient(...)) so the SDK doesn't rely on destructors; 2) explicitly await client.aclose() before the test ends (you are doing that but maybe destructor still runs later). Also try pinning httpx to 0.24.0 to see if httpcore change matters.

Mia Chen: tried async with too, still see the final "Event loop is closed" when pytest exits — looks like something registered on interpreter shutdown. :thinking:

Alex K.: ah, that matches an atexit handler. I remember a prior attempt to ensure clients get closed on process exit where we registered atexit.register(lambda: loop.run_until_complete(self.aclose())) — that will break when pytest/asyncio controls the loop. We should avoid using run_until_complete in atexit and instead schedule close tasks if a loop is running, or simply not register the handler at all and require explicit close/context manager.

Sam Ortega: agreed. Proposed fix: remove global atexit close; update __del__ to check asyncio.get_running_loop() and then call asyncio.create_task(self.aclose()) if possible, or fallback to logging a warning. Also add a fastapi dependency example in docs showing how to create one AsyncClient per app and close on shutdown event.

Mia Chen: fastapi/uvicorn users hit this too — if client is created at import time and then shutdown hooks try to run, mismatch happens. We should add a note in onboarding and the sample app repo.

Sam Ortega: I'll open an issue + PR with a small unit test that reproduces this pattern under pytest-asyncio and a patch that removes the atexit registration. /assign @alex_k

Dev Bot: Issue #2345 created: "async-sdk: avoid run_until_complete in atexit handler -> Event loop closed in pytest/notebooks" (labels: sdk, async, bug)

Alex K.: I'll take the PR review. Also add a changelog entry and a migration note: "If you relied on implicit close via process exit, call client.aclose() or use async with to avoid warnings."

Mia Chen: thanks! :thumbsup:
